headline: Charter stake write-down drives steep loss ahead of merger
summary_short: Liberty Broadband posted a $2,125 million net loss (diluted EPS -$14.86) in Q2 FY2026 after a $3.0 billion non-cash impairment on its Charter equity stake, taken on a sustained decline in Charter's share price; the holding company itself carries no revenue since the 2025 GCI divestiture.
summary_long: The $2,125 million net loss (diluted EPS -$14.86) was driven almost entirely by a $3.0 billion non-cash impairment on Liberty Broadband's equity-method investment in Charter, taken after a sustained, other-than-temporary decline in Charter's share price. Operating loss narrowed to $4 million from $10 million on lower deal-related professional fees. Interest expense fell to $23 million after Liberty Broadband retired its 3.125% debentures on April 6, 2026 using Margin Loan Facility proceeds and a $359 million Charter term loan. Cash fell to $43 million and long-term debt fell to $1,223 million on the debt retirement. No shares were repurchased, restricted by the pending Charter Combination; no guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Net loss driven by a $3.0 billion impairment on the Charter equity investment, taken after a sustained decline in Charter's share price that the company determined to be "other than temporary."
Swing to a $2,125 million net loss from $383 million net income was almost entirely the impairment; Charter's own standalone net income was roughly flat ($1,524M vs $1,495M).
Tracks the swing to a net loss; diluted share count was little changed at 144 million vs 143 million a year earlier, so per-share impact mirrors the net-income swing.
Consolidated operating loss improved $6 million "due to decreased professional service fees related to the Transactions."

Pretax loss of $2,792 million is the sum of the $2,653 million affiliate loss (impairment-driven), $23 million interest expense, and a $135 million dilution loss, partly offset by $20 million of financial-instrument gains.

Increased $2,998 million as the company recorded its $3.0 billion Charter impairment, reducing the investment to fair value using Charter's Level 1 share price; excess-basis amortization also runs through this line.
Not separately reconciled in the release; projected 2026 uses of cash cited are debt service, preferred dividends, and transaction-related expenses tied to the pending Combination.
Fell as the company retired all outstanding 3.125% Debentures due 2053 on April 6, 2026, paying $966 million including accrued interest, funded via the Margin Loan Facility and restricted cash.
Not explained in the release; the quarter also saw a $359 million Charter term loan advanced in May 2026 to repay Margin Loan Facility borrowings, but no line-item attribution is given.
Not separately reconciled beyond the quarter's net loss; the equity decline traces arithmetically to accumulated net losses, mostly this quarter's $2,125 million impairment-driven loss.
